clue.text: Hurry away after second snub

indicators.note: after says the hurrying-away piece follows the letter for second

parts.note: B stands for second, as in a B grade or second-class
to hurry is to rush
away means off, as in going off

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off after a moment, having been cold-shouldered.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff or curt dismissal of someone is a synonym of a snub.

clue.text: Carrying voice of a writer

definitions.meaning: a loud roar that carries a long way

explanation.surface: A novelist with a voice that carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud deep shout carries far; the Nobel-winning novelist Saul shares the surname.

clue.text: Replaced result in topcoat

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A changed outcome is found inside an overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose belted overcoat, a type of topcoat, named after the Irish province.

clue.text: Coming from such a wicked place north of the border

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A villain hails from some notorious town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: HAWICK is a Scottish Borders town; 'north of the border' means in Scotland as seen from England.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the Scottish Borders is an example of a place north of the English border.

clue.text: Herald gives warning of follower

parts.note: fore is the warning shout on a golf course
a shadow is someone who follows another closely

explanation.surface: A town crier announces something about a pursuer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald' is a verb here, not the messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to signal its coming, which is a synonym of hinting at it in advance.

clue.text: Spoil test with rodent

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: Ruining an experiment involving a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing animal of the squirrel family is an example of a rodent.

clue.text: Unspecified — a city west of this place

parts.note: NY is New York, the city
this place means here

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely places a city to the west of where they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning in any place at all, the word describes a location left unspecified.

clue.text: Homer with apt effect in figure of speech

indicators.note: with apt effect suggests the letters of the poet's name are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Homer uses an apt rhetorical figure to good effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling one thing another to suggest likeness is a common figure of speech.

clue.text: Barren girl taken out of dance

indicators.note: read as taken out(side) of, the girl is wrapped round the dance

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's heroine
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A lonely woman is removed from a dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out of' reads as removal, but it means placed outside: the girl wraps round the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Land without any trees is barren in the sense of bare or desolate.

clue.text: What one winds up with

parts.note: the closing remark of an argument or speech, the one you finish on

explanation.definitionFit: The final remark in a dispute is literally the one you wind up a speech with.

clue.text: Woman will make termly adjustments

indicators.note: making adjustments to the word termly rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A woman will tweak something every school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is a woman's name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Shed too much in cloudy conditions

definitions.meaning: to cast off too much, shedding to excess
weather with the sky covered in grey cloud

explanation.surface: A creature moults excessively in gloomy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey skies fully covered describe cloudy conditions; casting off too much is the punning first sense.

clue.text: Tea ladies initially interrupted by exercises in place of worship

indicators.note: interrupted by means the exercises break into the middle of the tea-and-ladies run

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of ladies

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Women's tea is disrupted by a workout in a church hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A small church or room for services is a place of worship.

clue.text: DIY learner in car committed the deed

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
committed means did
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A self-taught mechanic does the deed in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-taught is a do-it-yourself learner, a witty rendering of the term.

clue.text: Wholesome girl, you said, with vivacity — American?

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

indicators.note: said means the word is heard spoken

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U
brio is liveliness or vivacity
US means American

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lively, healthy girl you mentioned is from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Salubrious means health-giving, close in sense to wholesome.

clue.text: Vegetable as Easter offering? It's a frame-up

parts.note: an Easter egg is the traditional Easter gift
a plant is evidence placed to frame someone

explanation.surface: A vegetable given at Easter turns out to be planted evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is called by this name in America; it is an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: An afterthought: change last noisy old instrument

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
to alter is to change

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of noisy

explanation.surface: A note added later: swap out the final noisy old instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' is the indicator on 'noisy', not a word to rearrange after 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: The psaltery is an ancient plucked stringed instrument, so it is an example of an old instrument.

clue.text: Drug may cause stumbling in camels

indicators.note: stumbling suggests the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug might make camels stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescalin is a hallucinogen from the peyote cactus, an example of a drug.

clue.text: Snail, with flower circle, quietly accepted by deity

indicators.note: accepted by means taken into the deity, which goes round the rest

parts.note: a god is a deity
an aster is a daisy-like flower
O is the circle shape
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A snail with a flower garland is quietly received by a god.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an older spelling of gastropod.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is an example of this class of molluscs with a single muscular foot.

clue.text: Number Ten about to be occupied by Whitehead, the scientist?

indicators.note: occupied by means the reversed phrase holds the next letter inside it
about turns the whole number-ten phrase backwards

parts.note: ten as written
the head of White is its first letter, W

explanation.surface: Downing Street will be taken over by Whitehead, the scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten is the Prime Minister's Downing Street residence, and A. N. Whitehead was a philosopher; 'about' turns the whole phrase backwards before W goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac of that surname is the archetypal scientist; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Dutchman's to order a cab

parts.note: Hans is a typical Dutch or German man's name
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A Dutchman orders a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire was the Victorian cab.

clue.text: Employ alien in the fall

indicators.note: in means the alien goes inside the rain

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Hiring an alien in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fall' suggests autumn in American English; here it is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain someone, such as a lawyer, is to employ them.

clue.text: River bugs in force

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lice are small bugs

explanation.surface: Insects in an Italian river are present in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The police are a force, as in the Metropolitan Police Force.

clue.text: Learned a lot of rubbish about time

indicators.note: about means the trimmed rubbish goes round the time
a lot of means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: litter is rubbish
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Educated people spout plenty of nonsense about the age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' means most of the word, so the rubbish loses its last letter before splitting round the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means well read, a synonym of able to read and write well.

clue.text: Time-honoured substitute for gaoled

indicators.note: a substitute for the word gaoled uses the same letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Something venerable stands in for a jailed person.
explanation.definitionFit: Having existed for ages, something ancient is time-honoured.

clue.text: Musical composition by fat Asian

indicators.note: a composition is an arrangement, so the letters of fat Asian are composed into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of music written by a plump Asian person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical composition' reads as one definition, but 'composition' is the anagram signal; Disney's Fantasia is the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1940 Fantasia is an animated film set to classical music, a kind of musical.

clue.text: Irksome knotting around river

indicators.note: around means the knotting word goes round the river letter

parts.note: knotting means tying

explanation.surface: Tying knots by a river is tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying in the sense of testing one's patience is a synonym of irksome.

clue.text: A chancy entertainer

parts.note: a performer whose act involves taking risks, doing dangerous feats for film

explanation.definitionFit: A film double who performs dangerous feats takes chances to entertain.
